_comment: Known differences (AB-520): where the Java implementation may differ from the COBOL golden output. Only for quirks whose decision in the quirk register is 'fix', each linked to that decision. sign_off is 'pending' until the quirk owner approves; PARITY_REQUIRE_SIGNOFF=1 (go-live gate, ADR 0001) rejects pending entries. paths name the result paths that may differ (outcome.status, effects.count, effects[*].numbers.RISK_SCORE, effects[1].* ...); a whole-case '*' or effects[*].* is rejected so an unrelated cent difference in the same case still fails. The capability ticket narrows the paths further once its adapter exists.

differences.reason: 29 Feb expiry: Java computes a valid next-year expiry (recommended 28 Feb) instead of the invalid 20250229 that DB2 rejects; the policy update succeeds and the 'DB2 ERROR UPDATING RENEWAL' send and the partial update path (Q-07) disappear with it. That removes one effect and shifts the ones after it, hence effects[1..3]; the policy update's premium and renewal count must still match. AB-526 narrows this to the shifted fields once its adapter exists.
Zero-premium renewal: COBOL abends (S0CB) on the rate-change division and writes nothing; Java guards the division and completes. Only the outcome and the effect count may differ.
Java clamps negative scores to 0 and carries the full score in the queue message and map instead of the 3-digit truncation. Only the score fields may differ; the decision code must still match.

Java does not truncate the loss ratio, so a loss ratio of 1000% or more gets the +200 surcharge: the loss-ratio probe, the score and the band (decision code, reason, UW status) may differ. Policy number, dates, operations and SQLCODEs must still match.
Java keeps the accumulation reason; score and decision code must still match.

Java keeps the full loss ratio (1100.00) where the COBOL field drops the high-order digit (100.00). Both are above 80, so the surcharge, score, decision code and every write must still match; only the loss-ratio probe may differ.

A request that cannot be read is rejected before any write: Java sends only the 'ERROR RECEIVING UNDERWRITING DATA' text and returns, so the decision insert, POLICIES update, TD message and result map of the COBOL fall-through disappear and the remaining effects shift. Covers the whole effect list because the effect count changes; the outcome must still match.
